questions.prompt: A caller on WhatsApp video wears a police uniform and says you are under 'digital arrest'. Is that real?

options.text: No. Indian law has no such thing as a 'digital arrest' over a call
Yes, if they show a badge and agency logo behind them
options.explanationWrong: Uniforms, badges, and logos can be faked easily in a studio or screen backdrop.

options.text: Yes, unless you pay a verification deposit right away
options.explanationWrong: No real court or police agency asks you to pay money to avoid arrest.

options.text: Only if they warn you not to hang up or tell your family
options.explanationWrong: Forbidding you from speaking to family is a hallmark scam isolation tactic.

questions.explanationCorrect: There is no legal process called 'digital arrest' in India. Real officers never conduct arrests or court hearings on video calls.

questions.prompt: The video caller orders you: 'Do not disconnect the call and do not tell anyone.' Why?

options.text: Because video calls are faster than legal notices
options.explanationWrong: Real legal notices follow formal written procedures, not secret video calls.

options.text: To keep you panicked and stop family or friends from spotting the scam
Because telling someone makes the investigation invalid
options.explanationWrong: Scammers invent secrecy rules to prevent you from getting help.

options.text: To protect your bank balance automatically
options.explanationWrong: Staying isolated puts your money at higher risk, not lower.

questions.explanationCorrect: Isolation is the scammer's main tool. The moment you hang up and speak to someone you trust, their pressure loses power.

questions.prompt: The fake officer tells you to transfer ₹25,000 to a 'Reserve Bank verification account' to prove your innocence. What should you do?

options.text: Send half first so they know you are cooperating
options.explanationWrong: Sending any amount sends your savings straight to mule accounts.

options.text: Share your bank balance screenshot instead
options.explanationWrong: Never share sensitive financial balances with unknown video callers.

options.text: Refuse completely, hang up, and block the caller
Enter your UPI PIN to confirm your identity only
options.explanationWrong: A UPI PIN authorises money transfers—it never verifies innocence.

questions.explanationCorrect: Police, CBI, customs, and RBI never ask citizens to transfer money for verification or clearance.

questions.prompt: What is the safest immediate move when a stranger threatens you with arrest on a video call?

options.text: Keep your camera on while you search their badge number
options.explanationWrong: Staying on the call lets them escalate threats and keep you stressed.

options.text: Hang up immediately, block the number, and speak to a trusted person
Show them your Aadhaar card on camera to clear your name
options.explanationWrong: Showing identity documents on video gives scammers data for further misuse.

options.text: Download the remote-support app they recommend
options.explanationWrong: Remote-access apps let fraudsters watch your screen and steal OTPs.

questions.explanationCorrect: Disconnect right away, block the caller, and talk to a family member or trusted friend to break the panic.

questions.prompt: After hanging up on a fake CBI or cyber-police caller, how can you verify and report safely?

options.text: Call back the same WhatsApp number once you calm down
options.explanationWrong: Calling back reconnects you to the scammer.

options.text: Look up your local police station independently and report on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
Pay a legal agent advertised in a chat group
options.explanationWrong: Random agents online can be secondary scams.

options.text: Delete your call log and ignore it completely
options.explanationWrong: Keeping screenshots and reporting to 1930 helps trace and block scam accounts.

questions.explanationCorrect: Always verify through official directories or your local station, and report impersonation attempts on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.

questions.prompt: Which claim in an unknown video call is an immediate warning sign of an impersonation scam?

options.text: Demanding an immediate UPI or bank transfer to settle a criminal case online
Advising you to visit your nearest police station with written papers
options.explanationWrong: In-person verification at an official station is normal; secret online transfers are the trap.

options.text: Telling you that you have the right to speak to family or a lawyer
options.explanationWrong: Scammers forbid calling family; real procedures respect your rights.

options.text: Refusing to accept any money over the phone
options.explanationWrong: Real officials never demand money over calls.

questions.explanationCorrect: Any caller demanding instant transfers to 'settle' or 'verify' a legal case over a video call is a scammer.
